key_insight: Conditioning a recurrent forecasting model on temperature and thermal rate enables accurate prediction of grain growth under changing heat-treatment conditions.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce reliance on costly grain-growth simulations when assessing microstructure evolution during non-isothermal heat treatment.
method: Encode grain size distributions with a convolutional neural network.
Embed instantaneous temperature and thermal rate with a dedicated multilayer perceptron.
Forecast distribution evolution with a thermally conditioned recurrent network.
evidence_signal: Against validated front-tracking simulations, k-fold cross-validation yielded mean relative errors of 2.99% for one-hour cycles and 4.51% for four-hour cycles, with R² above 0.99; errors on ten simulations spanning four unseen thermal histories ranged from 1.91% to 14.66%.
watch_item: Evaluation is simulation-based, and the higher errors on some unseen thermal histories warrant caution when extending to new processing conditions.
paper_title: Thermally Conditioned Time-Series Forecasting of Grain Growth in Polycrystalline Materials
